purpose: Compare five existing frozen engine versions at fast, medium, and long practical search budgets; separate equal-budget competition from gains against a fixed opponent.

models.label: Original
models.description: Original handwritten evaluator with the unchanged production search

models.label: Neural 1,057
models.description: Previously verified residual 64-to-16-to-1 ReLU network, scale 0.5

models.label: Expanded 1,948
models.description: Selected before this tournament by lowest existing common validation loss among seeds 53, 71, and 89: 0.5174792042161678 at seed 89

round_robin.seed_policy: Ten disjoint blocks of 16 deals, one per unordered model pair; repeat each deal with swapped seating and reuse the block at all three time budgets. Original is always side B when present.

anchor.seed_policy: Reuse each learned-versus-original round-robin block and its 25 ms cell; add candidate 100/400 ms against original 25 ms. Original self-control uses its own 16-deal block at all three candidate budgets.

search.automatic_flip_depth: Production default: 5 below 80 ms, otherwise 6; determined separately from each player's time budget
search.other_settings: Unchanged arena defaults; no node cap or artificial game adjudication

execution.scheduling: Shuffle all 41 batches once with the fixed seed, then run six at a time
execution.stopping: Run all preregistered cells; no result-dependent stopping, retraining, model selection, or promotion

analysis.unit: Resample whole two-game deals independently within each of 11 deal blocks. Share each block's bootstrap indices across budgets and reused round-robin/anchor cells.
analysis.league_score: Equal-weight mean score against the other four models; win=1, draw=0.5, loss=0. Reverse each side-B result as 1 minus side-A score, preserving head-to-head dependence.
analysis.uncertainty: Pointwise 95% percentile bootstrap intervals; all rankings, pair comparisons, and time interactions are exploratory, without multiple-comparison correction.
analysis.claims: A league-score change measures relative standing as both sides receive more time. Fixed-opponent changes measure time gains. Do not infer an asymptotic ceiling or isolate parameter-count causality from these version comparisons.

limitations: Only 16 independent deals per head-to-head cell; modest differences will remain uncertain.
One frozen checkpoint per learned version; intervals cover deal variation, not training-seed variation.
Training datasets, objectives, and feature families differ across versions; this is not a controlled parameter-count scaling experiment.
Production automatic flip depth changes between 25 and 100 ms; these are practical budget comparisons rather than a fixed-search-policy intervention.
Wall-clock budgets run concurrently on one host. Record observed move times, nodes, and depths; some scheduling noise remains.
All time contrasts share deals, but each model pair uses a different deal block. Anchor model comparisons also use different blocks.
A small exploratory tournament does not replace the earlier independent, larger confirmation studies or establish a universal strongest engine.
